When working with sensitive data, it is important to use advanced encryption techniques to prevent a data breach. Key Protect uses the envelope encryption technique to keep your data resilient. Envelope encryption is the process of using encrypted keys, Data Encryption Keys and Root Keys, to protect your sensitive data.  Imagine that you plan to send a letter to a colleague. You want to discuss information that is highly sensitive, so you generate a secret code (Data Encryption Key) that is used to write (encrypt) the message in the letter. The letter is delivered to a mailbox (wrapped Data Encryption Key) that can only be opened by those with a copy of the mailbox key (Root key), including the colleague. Anyone who does not have an exact copy of the key will be unable to open the mailbox and see it's contents. When your colleague uses the key to unlock (unencrypt) the mailbox, they will need to know the secret code that the letter is written in to be able to understand the message. Everyone who is not aware of the secret code will conclude that the letter is a random mix of characters and will not be able to understand the letter's contents.  Data encryption keys (DEKs) are designed to encrypt your data and can be generated and managed by your service or an IBM Cloud service. rag_history_before_turn.content: How do cloud computing security protocols evolve over time, and what are the potential implications for restoring volumes from backup snapshots in IBM Cloud VPC?

I am unable to provide a comprehensive overview of the evolution of cloud computing security protocols over time, but I can inform you about specific security features and practices related to restoring volumes from backup snapshots in IBM Cloud VPC. These features include data inheritance, encryption, and cross-regional backup copies, all of which contribute to a more secure and resilient cloud computing environment. Backup snapshots can be utilized to restore volumes in a different region for business continuity or geographic expansion purposes. The restoration of volumes from backup snapshots can be performed through the UI, CLI, API, or Terraform. By using the backup service, you can regularly back up your volume data based on a schedule you set up, with the option to create backup snapshots as frequently as every hour.
What is Data Encryption?

Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) encrypt your data and can be created and managed by your service or an IBM Cloud service. In the context of IBM Cloud VPC, data encryption can be applied to block storage volumes using either IBM-managed encryption or customer-managed encryption. When restoring a volume from a backup snapshot, if the source volume used customer-managed encryption, the new volume will inherit that encryption with the original customer root key (CRK).

rag_history_before_turn.content: How do cloud computing security protocols evolve over time, and what are the potential implications for restoring volumes from backup snapshots in IBM Cloud VPC?

I am unable to provide a comprehensive overview of the evolution of cloud computing security protocols over time, but I can inform you about specific security features and practices related to restoring volumes from backup snapshots in IBM Cloud VPC. These features include data inheritance, encryption, and cross-regional backup copies, all of which contribute to a more secure and resilient cloud computing environment. Backup snapshots can be utilized to restore volumes in a different region for business continuity or geographic expansion purposes. The restoration of volumes from backup snapshots can be performed through the UI, CLI, API, or Terraform. By using the backup service, you can regularly back up your volume data based on a schedule you set up, with the option to create backup snapshots as frequently as every hour.
What is Data Encryption?

Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) encrypt your data and can be created and managed by your service or an IBM Cloud service. In the context of IBM Cloud VPC, data encryption can be applied to block storage volumes using either IBM-managed encryption or customer-managed encryption. When restoring a volume from a backup snapshot, if the source volume used customer-managed encryption, the new volume will inherit that encryption with the original customer root key (CRK).
It is the same as data backup and disaster recovery, right?

No, data encryption is not the same as data backup and disaster recovery. Encryption uses a two-way function to transform data into a form that hides its original value but can be converted back to the original state. On the other hand, the disaster recovery kit is an off-site and protected repository that includes hardware, software, and system secure configurations, as well as one-time keys and the disaster recovery plan. Meanwhile, data encryption keys are specifically designed to encrypt your data.

A VPC’s logical isolation is implemented by using virtual network functions and security features that give an enterprise customer granular control over which IP addresses or applications can access particular resources. About networking   IBM Cloud® Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) is a virtual network that is linked to your customer account. It gives you cloud security, with the ability to scale dynamically, by providing fine-grained control over your virtual infrastructure and your network traffic segmentation.     Overview   Each VPC is deployed to a single region. Within that region, the VPC can span multiple zones.  Subnets in your VPC can connect to the public internet through an optional public gateway. You can assign floating IP addresses to any virtual server instance to enable it to be reachable from the internet, independent of whether its subnet is attached to a public gateway.  Subnets within the VPC offer private connectivity; they can talk to each other over a private link through the implicit router. Setting up routes is not necessary. A VPC can span multiple zones within its assigned region.       Zones   A zone is an abstraction that refers to the physical data center that hosts the compute, network, and storage resources, plus the related cooling and power, which provides services and applications. Zones are isolated from each other to create no shared single point of failure, improved fault tolerance, and reduced latency. Each zone is assigned a default address prefix, which specifies the address range in which subnets can be created.

I am unable to provide a comprehensive overview of the evolution of cloud computing security protocols over time, but I can inform you about specific security features and practices related to restoring volumes from backup snapshots in IBM Cloud VPC. These features include data inheritance, encryption, and cross-regional backup copies, all of which contribute to a more secure and resilient cloud computing environment. Backup snapshots can be utilized to restore volumes in a different region for business continuity or geographic expansion purposes. The restoration of volumes from backup snapshots can be performed through the UI, CLI, API, or Terraform. By using the backup service, you can regularly back up your volume data based on a schedule you set up, with the option to create backup snapshots as frequently as every hour.
What is Data Encryption?

Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) encrypt your data and can be created and managed by your service or an IBM Cloud service. In the context of IBM Cloud VPC, data encryption can be applied to block storage volumes using either IBM-managed encryption or customer-managed encryption. When restoring a volume from a backup snapshot, if the source volume used customer-managed encryption, the new volume will inherit that encryption with the original customer root key (CRK).
It is the same as data backup and disaster recovery, right?

No, data encryption is not the same as data backup and disaster recovery. Encryption uses a two-way function to transform data into a form that hides its original value but can be converted back to the original state. Meanwhile, data encryption keys are specifically designed to encrypt your data.

Virtual Servers for VPC is an Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) offering that provides the benefits of VPC, including network isolation, security, and flexibility. This flexibility allows you to customize the system according to your specific needs, giving you control over your infrastructure.
With Virtual Servers for VPC, you can quickly provision instances with high network performance. When you provision an instance, you select a profile that matches the amount of memory and computing power needed for the application you plan to run. Instances are available on the x86 architecture.
IBM Cloud® Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) allows you to establish your virtual private cloud by defining a virtual network that is logically isolated from all other public cloud tenants. The software-defined networking (SDN) and virtual network functions allow you to quickly establish the network constructs and on-prem connectivity needed to run your workload.
Hyper Protect Virtual Servers for VPC takes advantage of IBM Secure Execution for Linux to provide a boundary around each instance, offering protection from internal and external threats. It provides the following benefits:
- Secure Execution boundary for protection from internal and external threats
- Technical assurance that unauthorized users, including IBM Cloud admins, do not have access to the application
- Individual, instance-level secure boundaries lock down workloads
- Multiparty contract and attestation of deployment
- Zero Trust principles from workload development through deployment.
